subject: Design proposal: On-prem KMS egress-minimization & split-witness
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moroz <elena.moroz@greenleaf.com>, Michael Dawson <michael.dawson@greenleaf.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Design proposal: On-prem KMS egress-minimization & split-witness

Hi Elena / Michael,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our call, attached is a focused proposal for the Greenleaf on-prem KMS integration with two goals: (1) ensure zero key-material egress from the customer HSM and (2) provide a split-witness model for emergency unseal that meets your compliance requirements.

High level:
- BYOK model where the customer's HSM holds the root key and performs all unwrapping/signing operations.
- Redwood runtime runs inside your VPC with private peering; we never persist raw key material.
- We propose a split-witness escrow: two geographically separate custodians (one customer, one neutral third-party) each hold a share of an unseal key; no single party can reconstruct.
- Minimal egress surface: all telemetry and audit events are forwarded via an encrypted push channel; wrapped tokens only (no raw keys) leave HSM.

Attachments: kms-circuit-diagram.png, split-witness-proposal-v1.pdf, network-zone-matrix.xlsx

Open questions for design review:
1) Are the proposed custodians for the split-witness acceptable (Greenleaf security + SecureCustody LLP)?
2) Rotation cadence expectations: 90 days automated rotation vs 30 days for high-risk tenants?
3) Disaster recovery: acceptable emergency unseal workflow and audit evidence required?

Please review the proposal and the diagram. Suggested reviewers from Redwood: Laura for network gating, Marcus for ops/rotation automation, Soojin for HSM integration details.

If this looks reasonable, I’ll schedule a 60-min design review with your security and infra leads next week and circulate a pre-read.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Moroz <elena.moroz@greenleaf.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Michael Dawson <michael.dawson@greenleaf.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Design proposal: On-prem KMS egress-minimization & split-witness

Jordan —

Thanks for the proposal and the diagram. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before the review: 

- Audit evidence: we need a tamper-evident trail for every unseal and rotation event. Can Redwood ingest HSM audit logs and keep a copy in our VPC without exposing key material?
- Failover: if the Redwood runtime can’t reach the HSM (network partition), what’s the app-level fallback? Can wrapped tokens be replayed for short windows?
- Split-witness legal: SecureCustody LLP is acceptable, but we need an SLA for availability during an emergency ceremony. Can we see their standard contract?
- Rotation: 90 days is okay for most keys, but any customer-triggered emergency rotation needs to be supported within an hour. Is there a manual API for emergency key roll-forward?

Also: we prefer the custodians to be resident in different cloud zones. Your diagram labels are a little dense — could you extract the minimal path that shows "no egress of raw keys" for our auditors?

—Elena
Elena Moroz
Head of Cloud Security, Greenleaf Financial

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moroz <elena.moroz@greenleaf.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Michael Dawson <michael.dawson@greenleaf.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Design proposal: On-prem KMS egress-minimization & split-witness

Thanks Jordan — quick notes from a networking perspective.

1) Private connectivity: recommend dedicated Private Interconnect or AWS Direct Connect (or equivalent), not a single-socket VPN. Peering should be configured to limit routes to only the subnets hosting the Redwood runtime and monitoring endpoints.

2) Egress control: implement strict egress ACLs on the HSM subnet that only permit:
   - mTLS to Redwood runtime endpoints over private IPs
   - outbound to SecureCustody LLP for remote key-witnessing (only to their audited endpoints)

3) Telemetry & logs: audit-forwarder should push logs to your SIEM over a dedicated, encrypted channel. For compliance, we can sign each audit bundle with the HSM so integrity is provable without exposing key material.

4) Token caching: ops note — allow short-lived wrapped token caching at the runtime layer (TTL 30s–2m) to absorb brief HSM unavailability while preventing replay windows. Cache should be in-memory and flushed on failover.

5) NAT & egress minimization: avoid customer NAT for egress whenever possible. If NAT is unavoidable, tag egress flows and restrict them at the firewall to only the wrapped-token endpoints.

I can sketch a simplified diagram showing just the minimum proof channel for auditors; Jordan, Marcus — do you want me to produce that before the review?

-laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Network Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Moroz <elena.moroz@greenleaf.com>, Michael Dawson <michael.dawson@greenleaf.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Design proposal: On-prem KMS egress-minimization & split-witness

Looping in ops perspective and proposed runbook items.

Operations thoughts:
- Rotation automation: Redwood will provide a rotation runner that triggers HSM rotation via the customer's management API and rotates wrapped-key material in the runtime. Default cadence: 90 days, configurable per-tenant.
- Emergency rotation: provide manual API (authenticated to Greenleaf security SSO) that initiates a fast rotation and invalidates active session tokens. We'll document an "emergency rotation" playbook with steps and who to call at SecureCustody.
- Snapshots & escrow: periodic sealed snapshots (encrypted with a split-witness layer) retained only within Greenleaf's storage buckets. Snapshots are integrity-signed by the HSM and include a full audit index.
- DR rehearsals: recommend quarterly DR rehearsals involving both custodians. During rehearsals, unseal flows will be exercised in a read-only audit mode to avoid exposure.

Operational ask for Greenleaf: grant the Redwood ops service account limited management API rights to call rotation endpoints and to query HSM audit logs (read-only). All actions will be logged and forwarded to your SIEM.

I can attach a draft runbook after the design review. Also attaching a short checklist for the emergency unseal ceremony (see split-witness-proposal-v1.pdf).

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
